title: runtime: add pinned benchmark profile + default flags for public latency/$ runs
author: Keiko Yamamoto
description:
Motivation: our latency/$ report needs run-to-run and region-to-region consistency. Over the last few weeks we saw small drift caused by runtime defaults changing (adaptive batching heuristics, cache reuse behavior, and auto-tuning). This PR introduces an explicit, versioned benchmark runtime profile and wires it into the server so benchmark windows can pin a stable set of flags without impacting production defaults.

What changed (high level): adds `--runtime.profile=public_benchmark_v1` (and env `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_PROFILE`) that applies a curated set of runtime config overrides used during benchmark windows; keeps existing production defaults unchanged when profile is not set; emits the resolved profile + pinned flags into server startup logs and `/healthz/config` so benchmark-lab can record the exact effective settings.

Pinned settings in public_benchmark_v1 (summary): disables adaptive micro-batching target updates during the run (uses fixed `scheduler.max_wait_ms` and fixed `max_batch_tokens`), pins prefix/KV cache behavior to conservative reuse + deterministic eviction, disables background auto-tuning of attention kernels after warmup, standardizes prefill chunking thresholds, and turns on an explicit cache reset hook that benchmark-lab can call between runs (so caching policy matches the methodology, not the prior run history).

Notes: this is intentionally scoped to the benchmark windows and the harness. We are not claiming these are the best defaults for all customer workloads. The goal is repeatability + clear disclosure.

Follow-ups: benchmark-lab will set `--runtime.profile=public_benchmark_v1` for all region runners and will persist the `/healthz/config` snapshot in artifacts (tracked in ENG-2860).
commits: runtime/config: add RuntimeProfile enum and config overlay plumbing
runtime/scheduler: make adaptive batch target updates opt-in for benchmark profile
runtime/cache: add deterministic eviction + cache reset endpoint hook
runtime/server: expose resolved config snapshot in /healthz/config (sanitized)
docs/internal: describe public_benchmark_v1 profile and intended use
illustrative_snippet:
New flag and profile selection:

  --runtime.profile=public_benchmark_v1

Applied overlay (excerpt):

  scheduler.max_wait_ms=2
  scheduler.max_batch_tokens=8192
  scheduler.adaptive_batching=false
  cache.kv.reuse_policy=conservative
  cache.kv.eviction_policy=fifo
  autotune.enable_background=false
  prefill.chunk_tokens=2048

Server startup log now includes:

  runtime_profile=public_benchmark_v1 resolved_flags_hash=sha256:…
review_conversation: Ravi Menon: Can we make sure this doesn’t silently change prod behavior? I’m worried someone sets the env var globally in a deployment template.

Keiko Yamamoto (author): Agree. Kept prod defaults as-is; profile is only applied when `--runtime.profile` is explicitly set. Also added a startup WARN line when a profile != default is used (so it’s noisy in logs).
Neha Kapoor: From an SRE perspective I like pinning the knobs, but the cache reset hook—can it be abused / cause load spikes if called too frequently?

Keiko Yamamoto (author): Good call. Added rate limiting (1 reset / 60s) and it’s disabled unless `runtime.profile` is set to a benchmark profile. Also emits a metric `runtime_cache_reset_total` for guardrails.
Claire Dubois: For methodology: we need to be explicit whether prefix caching is enabled between requests within a run but not across runs. Can we guarantee the harness can reset between runs?

Keiko Yamamoto (author): Yes. The hook is a lightweight endpoint that clears prefix/KV caches and resets per-run counters. benchmark-lab will call it between runs; within a run cache behavior stays enabled according to the pinned settings.
Peter Holtz: Please add a config snapshot endpoint to capture the *effective* values after overlays. Otherwise marketing will copy the intended values and we’ll miss edge cases.

Keiko Yamamoto (author): Added `/healthz/config` that returns a sanitized list of resolved config values + profile name + flags hash; excludes secrets/keys. Also included it in startup logs for easy artifact capture.
Ravi Menon: One more thing: disabling background auto-tune may shift absolute performance on some GPUs. Are we comfortable disclosing that in the report appendix?
Claire Dubois: Yes, the point is repeatability. We’ll disclose in the methodology that auto-tune is disabled after warmup to avoid mid-run drift.
Neha Kapoor: Approved once rate limit + profile gating landed.
Ravi Menon: Approved. Thanks for keeping it explicit and versioned.
release_notes: Internal-only: introduces `--runtime.profile=public_benchmark_v1` for benchmark window consistency; no change to production defaults unless profile is explicitly enabled.
